previous_assumption: The auth flow (scrypt hashing, timing-safe compare, hashed session tokens) was believed complete/production-safe once those three properties were in place.
correction: A dedicated security-audit subagent pass found two real, fixable Low-severity gaps that unit tests never would have caught: (1) AuthService.login only ran the slow scrypt verify when the user existed (short-circuit on `!user`), letting an attacker enumerate valid emails via response-time measurement even though the error message was identical — fixed by always verifying against a fixed DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH when no user is found. (2) No rate limiting existed on /auth/login or /auth/signup at all — added @fastify/rate-limit registered with global:false, opted into only by those two routes (10/min per IP), verified live (11th rapid attempt returns 429). Also found and fixed, while auditing: MachineRepository.create was the only insert-with-a-unique-constraint in the codebase that didn't translate a 23505 violation to ConflictError (a robustness gap, not a security hole, but inconsistent with the pattern everywhere else). General lesson: authorization/IDOR coverage was fully clean across all 14 services (verified via a deep, deliberate ownership-check audit) — the actual gaps were in auth-adjacent infra (timing, rate limiting) that a pure code-logic review of "does every service check ownership" doesn't surface. A full security pass needs to explicitly check auth/session timing and abuse-resistance as its own category, not just authorization logic.
